|**aggregationInterval**|"AGGREGATION_INTERVAL_UNSPECIFIED" | "INTERVAL_5_SEC" | "INTERVAL_30_SEC" | "INTERVAL_1_MIN" | "INTERVAL_5_MIN" | "INTERVAL_10_MIN" | "INTERVAL_15_MIN"|Optional. The aggregation interval for the logs. Default value is INTERVAL_5_SEC.||
|**description**|str|Optional. The user-supplied description of the VPC Flow Logs configuration. Maximum of 512 characters.||
|**filterExpr**|str|Optional. Export filter used to define which VPC Flow Logs should be logged.||
|**flowSampling**|float|Optional. The value of the field must be in (0, 1]. The sampling rate of VPC Flow Logs where 1.0 means all collected logs are reported. Setting the sampling rate to 0.0 is not allowed. If you want to disable VPC Flow Logs, use the state field instead. Default value is 1.0.||
|**interconnectAttachmentRef**|[NetworkmanagementCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1NetworkManagementVPCFlowLogsConfigSpecInterconnectAttachmentRef](#networkmanagementcnrmcloudgooglecomv1alpha1networkmanagementvpcflowlogsconfigspecinterconnectattachmentref)|interconnect attachment ref||

|**metadataFields**|[str]|Optional. Custom metadata fields to include in the reported VPC flow logs. Can only be specified if "metadata" was set to CUSTOM_METADATA.||

### OrgpolicyCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1OrgPolicyPolicySpecDryRunSpecRulesItems0Condition

A condition which determines whether this rule is used in the evaluation of the policy. When set, the `expression` field in the `Expr' must include from 1 to 10 subexpressions, joined by the "\|\|" or "&&" operators. Each subexpression must be of the form "resource.matchTag('<ORG_ID>/tag_key_short_name, 'tag_value_short_name')". or "resource.matchTagId('tagKeys/key_id', 'tagValues/value_id')". where key_name and value_name are the resource names for Label Keys and Values. These names are available from the Tag Manager Service. An example expression is: "resource.matchTag('123456789/environment, 'prod')". or "resource.matchTagId('tagKeys/123', 'tagValues/456')".

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**description**|str|Optional. Description of the expression. This is a longer text which describes the expression, e.g. when hovered over it in a UI.||
|**expression**|str|Textual representation of an expression in Common Expression Language syntax.||
|**location**|str|Optional. String indicating the location of the expression for error reporting, e.g. a file name and a position in the file.||
|**title**|str|Optional. Title for the expression, i.e. a short string describing its purpose. This can be used e.g. in UIs which allow to enter the expression.||

### OsconfigCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1OSConfigPatchDeploymentSpecRolloutDisruptionBudget

Immutable. The maximum number (or percentage) of VMs per zone to disrupt at any given moment. The number of VMs calculated from multiplying the percentage by the total number of VMs in a zone is rounded up. During patching, a VM is considered disrupted from the time the agent is notified to begin until patching has completed. This disruption time includes the time to complete reboot and any post-patch steps. A VM contributes to the disruption budget if its patching operation fails either when applying the patches, running pre or post patch steps, or if it fails to respond with a success notification before timing out. VMs that are not running or do not have an active agent do not count toward this disruption budget. For zone-by-zone rollouts, if the disruption budget in a zone is exceeded, the patch job stops, because continuing to the next zone requires completion of the patch process in the previous zone. For example, if the disruption budget has a fixed value of 10, and 8 VMs fail to patch in the current zone, the patch job continues to patch 2 VMs at a time until the zone is completed. When that zone is completed successfully, patching begins with 10 VMs at a time in the next zone. If 10 VMs in the next zone fail to patch, the patch job stops.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**fixed**|int|Immutable. Specifies a fixed value.||
|**percentage**|int|Immutable. Specifies the relative value defined as a percentage, which will be multiplied by a reference value.||

### PubsubCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1PubSubSnapshotSpecPubSubSubscriptionRef

The subscription whose backlog the snapshot retains. Specifically, the created snapshot is guaranteed to retain: (a) The existing backlog on the subscription. More precisely, this is defined as the messages in the subscription's backlog that are unacknowledged upon the successful completion of the snapshots.create request; as well as: (b) Any messages published to the subscription's topic following the successful completion of the snapshots.create request. Format is projects/{project}/subscriptions/{sub}.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**external**|str|A reference to an externally managed PubSubSubscription resource. Should be in the format "projects/{{projectID}}/subscriptions/{{subscriptionID}}".||
|**name**|str|The name of a PubSubSubscription resource.||
|**namespace**|str|The namespace of a PubSubSubscription resource.||

|**expireTime**|str|Optional. The snapshot is guaranteed to exist up until this time. A newly-created snapshot expires no later than 7 days from the time of its creation. Its exact lifetime is determined at creation by the existing backlog in the source subscription. Specifically, the lifetime of the snapshot is `7 days - (age of oldest unacked message in the subscription)`. For example, consider a subscription whose oldest unacked message is 3 days old. If a snapshot is created from this subscription, the snapshot -- which will always capture this 3-day-old backlog as long as the snapshot exists -- will expire in 4 days. The service will refuse to create a snapshot that would expire in less than 1 hour after creation.||

### RedisCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1RedisClusterStatusObservedStateCrossClusterReplicationConfigMembership

Output only. An output only view of all the member clusters participating in the cross cluster replication. This view will be provided by every member cluster irrespective of its cluster role(primary or secondary).  A primary cluster can provide information about all the secondary clusters replicating from it. However, a secondary cluster only knows about the primary cluster from which it is replicating. However, for scenarios, where the primary cluster is unavailable(e.g. regional outage), a GetCluster request can be sent to any other member cluster and this field will list all the member clusters participating in cross cluster replication.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

|**secondaryClusters**|[[RedisCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1RedisClusterStatusObservedStateCrossClusterReplicationConfigMembershipSecondaryClustersItems0](#rediscnrmcloudgooglecomv1alpha1redisclusterstatusobservedstatecrossclusterreplicationconfigmembershipsecondaryclustersitems0)]|Output only. The list of secondary clusters replicating from the primary cluster.||

Specifies the KMS configuration for the one or more keys used to<br />protect the backup. Values are of the form<br />`projects/<project>/locations/<location>/keyRings/<key_ring>/cryptoKeys/<kms_key_name>`.<br /><br />The keys referenced by kms_key_names must fully cover all<br />regions of the backup's instance configuration. Some examples:<br />* For single region instance configs, specify a single regional<br />location KMS key.<br />* For multi-regional instance configs of type GOOGLE_MANAGED,<br />either specify a multi-regional location KMS key or multiple regional<br />location KMS keys that cover all regions in the instance config.<br />* For an instance config of type USER_MANAGED, please specify only<br />regional location KMS keys to cover each region in the instance config.<br />Multi-regional location KMS keys are not supported for USER_MANAGED<br />instance configs.||

Examples of valid cron specifications:<br />* `0 2/12 * * * ` : every 12 hours at (2, 14) hours past midnight in UTC.<br />* `0 2,14 * * * ` : every 12 hours at (2,14) hours past midnight in UTC.<br />* `0 2 * * * `    : once a day at 2 past midnight in UTC.<br />* `0 2 * * 0 `    : once a week every Sunday at 2 past midnight in UTC.<br />* `0 2 8 * * `    : once a month on 8th day at 2 past midnight in UTC.||

### StorageinsightsCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1StorageInsightsDatasetConfigSpecCloudStorageObjectRef

Input only. Optional. Cloud Storage object containing a list of project or folder numbers to include in the dataset; it cannot contain a mix of project and folders.  The object must be a text file where each line has one of the following entries: - Project number, formatted as `projects/{project_number}`, for example, `projects/1234567890`. - Folder identifier, formatted as `folders/{folder_number}`, for example, `folders/9876543210`.

### TranscoderCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1TranscoderJobSpecConfigElementaryStreamsItems0VideoStreamH264

H264 codec settings.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**allowOpenGop**|bool|Specifies whether an open Group of Pictures (GOP) structure should be allowed or not. The default is `false`.||
|**aqStrength**|float|Specify the intensity of the adaptive quantizer (AQ). Must be between 0 and 1, where 0 disables the quantizer and 1 maximizes the quantizer. A higher value equals a lower bitrate but smoother image. The default is 0.||
|**bFrameCount**|int|The number of consecutive B-frames. Must be greater than or equal to zero. Must be less than [H264CodecSettings.gop_frame_count][google.cloud.video.transcoder.v1.VideoStream.H264CodecSettings.gop_frame_count] if set. The default is 0.||
|**bPyramid**|bool|Allow B-pyramid for reference frame selection. This may not be supported on all decoders. The default is `false`.||
|**bitrateBps**|int|Required. The video bitrate in bits per second. The minimum value is 1,000. The maximum value is 800,000,000.||
|**crfLevel**|int|Target CRF level. Must be between 10 and 36, where 10 is the highest quality and 36 is the most efficient compression. The default is 21.||
|**enableTwoPass**|bool|Use two-pass encoding strategy to achieve better video quality. [H264CodecSettings.rate_control_mode][google.cloud.video.transcoder.v1.VideoStream.H264CodecSettings.rate_control_mode] must be `vbr`. The default is `false`.||
|**entropyCoder**|str|The entropy coder to use. The default is `cabac`.<br /><br />Supported entropy coders:<br /><br />- `cavlc`<br />- `cabac`||
|**frameRate**|float|Required. The target video frame rate in frames per second (FPS). Must be less than or equal to 120.||
|**frameRateConversionStrategy**|str|Optional. Frame rate conversion strategy for desired frame rate. The default is `DOWNSAMPLE`.||
|**gopDuration**|str|Select the GOP size based on the specified duration. The default is `3s`. Note that `gopDuration` must be less than or equal to [`segmentDuration`](#SegmentSettings), and [`segmentDuration`](#SegmentSettings) must be divisible by `gopDuration`.||
|**gopFrameCount**|int|Select the GOP size based on the specified frame count. Must be greater than zero.||
|**heightPixels**|int|The height of the video in pixels. Must be an even integer.<br />When not specified, the height is adjusted to match the specified width<br />and input aspect ratio. If both are omitted, the input height is used.<br /><br />For portrait videos that contain horizontal ASR and rotation metadata,<br />provide the height, in pixels, per the horizontal ASR. The API calculates<br />the width per the horizontal ASR. The API detects any rotation metadata<br />and swaps the requested height and width for the output.||
|**hlg**|any|Optional. HLG color format setting for H264.||
|**pixelFormat**|str|Pixel format to use. The default is `yuv420p`.<br /><br />Supported pixel formats:<br /><br />- `yuv420p` pixel format<br />- `yuv422p` pixel format<br />- `yuv444p` pixel format<br />- `yuv420p10` 10-bit HDR pixel format<br />- `yuv422p10` 10-bit HDR pixel format<br />- `yuv444p10` 10-bit HDR pixel format<br />- `yuv420p12` 12-bit HDR pixel format<br />- `yuv422p12` 12-bit HDR pixel format<br />- `yuv444p12` 12-bit HDR pixel format||
|**preset**|str|Enforces the specified codec preset. The default is `veryfast`. The available options are [FFmpeg-compatible](https://trac.ffmpeg.org/wiki/Encode/H.264#Preset). Note that certain values for this field may cause the transcoder to override other fields you set in the `H264CodecSettings` message.||
|**profile**|str|Enforces the specified codec profile. The following profiles are<br />supported:<br /><br />*   `baseline`<br />*   `main`<br />*   `high` (default)<br /><br />The available options are<br />[FFmpeg-compatible](https://trac.ffmpeg.org/wiki/Encode/H.264#Tune).<br />Note that certain values for this field may cause the<br />transcoder to override other fields you set in the `H264CodecSettings`<br />message.||
|**rateControlMode**|str|Specify the mode. The default is `vbr`.<br /><br />Supported rate control modes:<br /><br />- `vbr` - variable bitrate<br />- `crf` - constant rate factor||
|**sdr**|any|Optional. SDR color format setting for H264.||
|**tune**|str|Enforces the specified codec tune. The available options are [FFmpeg-compatible](https://trac.ffmpeg.org/wiki/Encode/H.264#Tune). Note that certain values for this field may cause the transcoder to override other fields you set in the `H264CodecSettings` message.||
|**vbvFullnessBits**|int|Initial fullness of the Video Buffering Verifier (VBV) buffer in bits. Must be greater than zero. The default is equal to 90% of [H264CodecSettings.vbv_size_bits][google.cloud.video.transcoder.v1.VideoStream.H264CodecSettings.vbv_size_bits].||
|**vbvSizeBits**|int|Size of the Video Buffering Verifier (VBV) buffer in bits. Must be greater than zero. The default is equal to [H264CodecSettings.bitrate_bps][google.cloud.video.transcoder.v1.VideoStream.H264CodecSettings.bitrate_bps].||
|**widthPixels**|int|The width of the video in pixels. Must be an even integer.<br />When not specified, the width is adjusted to match the specified height<br />and input aspect ratio. If both are omitted, the input width is used.<br /><br />For portrait videos that contain horizontal ASR and rotation metadata,<br />provide the width, in pixels, per the horizontal ASR. The API calculates<br />the height per the horizontal ASR. The API detects any rotation metadata<br />and swaps the requested height and width for the output.||

|**aqStrength**|float|Specify the intensity of the adaptive quantizer (AQ). Must be between 0 and 1, where 0 disables the quantizer and 1 maximizes the quantizer. A higher value equals a lower bitrate but smoother image. The default is 0.||
|**bFrameCount**|int|The number of consecutive B-frames. Must be greater than or equal to zero. Must be less than [H265CodecSettings.gop_frame_count][google.cloud.video.transcoder.v1.VideoStream.H265CodecSettings.gop_frame_count] if set. The default is 0.||
|**bPyramid**|bool|Allow B-pyramid for reference frame selection. This may not be supported on all decoders. The default is `false`.||
|**bitrateBps**|int|Required. The video bitrate in bits per second. The minimum value is 1,000. The maximum value is 800,000,000.||
|**crfLevel**|int|Target CRF level. Must be between 10 and 36, where 10 is the highest quality and 36 is the most efficient compression. The default is 21.||
|**enableTwoPass**|bool|Use two-pass encoding strategy to achieve better video quality. [H265CodecSettings.rate_control_mode][google.cloud.video.transcoder.v1.VideoStream.H265CodecSettings.rate_control_mode] must be `vbr`. The default is `false`.||
|**frameRate**|float|Required. The target video frame rate in frames per second (FPS). Must be less than or equal to 120.||
|**frameRateConversionStrategy**|str|Optional. Frame rate conversion strategy for desired frame rate. The default is `DOWNSAMPLE`.||
|**gopDuration**|str|Select the GOP size based on the specified duration. The default is `3s`. Note that `gopDuration` must be less than or equal to [`segmentDuration`](#SegmentSettings), and [`segmentDuration`](#SegmentSettings) must be divisible by `gopDuration`.||
|**gopFrameCount**|int|Select the GOP size based on the specified frame count. Must be greater than zero.||
|**hdr10**|any|Optional. HDR10 color format setting for H265.||
|**heightPixels**|int|The height of the video in pixels. Must be an even integer.<br />When not specified, the height is adjusted to match the specified width<br />and input aspect ratio. If both are omitted, the input height is used.<br /><br />For portrait videos that contain horizontal ASR and rotation metadata,<br />provide the height, in pixels, per the horizontal ASR. The API calculates<br />the width per the horizontal ASR. The API detects any rotation metadata<br />and swaps the requested height and width for the output.||
|**hlg**|any|Optional. HLG color format setting for H265.||
|**pixelFormat**|str|Pixel format to use. The default is `yuv420p`.<br /><br />Supported pixel formats:<br /><br />- `yuv420p` pixel format<br />- `yuv422p` pixel format<br />- `yuv444p` pixel format<br />- `yuv420p10` 10-bit HDR pixel format<br />- `yuv422p10` 10-bit HDR pixel format<br />- `yuv444p10` 10-bit HDR pixel format<br />- `yuv420p12` 12-bit HDR pixel format<br />- `yuv422p12` 12-bit HDR pixel format<br />- `yuv444p12` 12-bit HDR pixel format||
|**preset**|str|Enforces the specified codec preset. The default is `veryfast`. The available options are [FFmpeg-compatible](https://trac.ffmpeg.org/wiki/Encode/H.265). Note that certain values for this field may cause the transcoder to override other fields you set in the `H265CodecSettings` message.||
|**profile**|str|Enforces the specified codec profile. The following profiles are<br />supported:<br /><br />*   8-bit profiles<br />*   `main` (default)<br />*   `main-intra`<br />*   `mainstillpicture`<br />*   10-bit profiles<br />*   `main10` (default)<br />*   `main10-intra`<br />*   `main422-10`<br />*   `main422-10-intra`<br />*   `main444-10`<br />*   `main444-10-intra`<br />*   12-bit profiles<br />*   `main12` (default)<br />*   `main12-intra`<br />*   `main422-12`<br />*   `main422-12-intra`<br />*   `main444-12`<br />*   `main444-12-intra`<br /><br />The available options are<br />[FFmpeg-compatible](https://x265.readthedocs.io/).<br />Note that certain values for this field may cause the<br />transcoder to override other fields you set in the `H265CodecSettings`<br />message.||
|**rateControlMode**|str|Specify the mode. The default is `vbr`.<br /><br />Supported rate control modes:<br /><br />- `vbr` - variable bitrate<br />- `crf` - constant rate factor||
|**sdr**|any|Optional. SDR color format setting for H265.||
|**tune**|str|Enforces the specified codec tune. The available options are [FFmpeg-compatible](https://trac.ffmpeg.org/wiki/Encode/H.265). Note that certain values for this field may cause the transcoder to override other fields you set in the `H265CodecSettings` message.||
|**vbvFullnessBits**|int|Initial fullness of the Video Buffering Verifier (VBV) buffer in bits. Must be greater than zero. The default is equal to 90% of [H265CodecSettings.vbv_size_bits][google.cloud.video.transcoder.v1.VideoStream.H265CodecSettings.vbv_size_bits].||
|**vbvSizeBits**|int|Size of the Video Buffering Verifier (VBV) buffer in bits. Must be greater than zero. The default is equal to `VideoStream.bitrate_bps`.||
|**widthPixels**|int|The width of the video in pixels. Must be an even integer.<br />When not specified, the width is adjusted to match the specified height<br />and input aspect ratio. If both are omitted, the input width is used.<br /><br />For portrait videos that contain horizontal ASR and rotation metadata,<br />provide the width, in pixels, per the horizontal ASR. The API calculates<br />the height per the horizontal ASR. The API detects any rotation metadata<br />and swaps the requested height and width for the output.||

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**columnCount**|int|The maximum number of sprites per row in a sprite sheet. The default is 0, which indicates no maximum limit.||
|**endTimeOffset**|str|End time in seconds, relative to the output file timeline. When `end_time_offset` is not specified, the sprites are generated until the end of the output file.||
|**filePrefix**|str|Required. File name prefix for the generated sprite sheets.<br /><br />Each sprite sheet has an incremental 10-digit zero-padded suffix starting<br />from 0 before the extension, such as `sprite_sheet0000000123.jpeg`.||
|**format**|str|Format type. The default is `jpeg`.<br /><br />Supported formats:<br /><br />- `jpeg`||
|**interval**|str|Starting from `0s`, create sprites at regular intervals. Specify the interval value in seconds.||
|**quality**|int|The quality of the generated sprite sheet. Enter a value between 1 and 100, where 1 is the lowest quality and 100 is the highest quality. The default is 100. A high quality value corresponds to a low image data compression ratio.||
|**rowCount**|int|The maximum number of rows per sprite sheet. When the sprite sheet is full, a new sprite sheet is created. The default is 0, which indicates no maximum limit.||
|**spriteHeightPixels**|int|Required. The height of sprite in pixels. Must be an even integer. To<br />preserve the source aspect ratio, set the<br />[SpriteSheet.sprite_height_pixels][google.cloud.video.transcoder.v1.SpriteSheet.sprite_height_pixels]<br />field or the<br />[SpriteSheet.sprite_width_pixels][google.cloud.video.transcoder.v1.SpriteSheet.sprite_width_pixels]<br />field, but not both (the API will automatically calculate the missing<br />field).<br /><br />For portrait videos that contain horizontal ASR and rotation metadata,<br />provide the height, in pixels, per the horizontal ASR. The API calculates<br />the width per the horizontal ASR. The API detects any rotation metadata<br />and swaps the requested height and width for the output.||
|**spriteWidthPixels**|int|Required. The width of sprite in pixels. Must be an even integer. To<br />preserve the source aspect ratio, set the<br />[SpriteSheet.sprite_width_pixels][google.cloud.video.transcoder.v1.SpriteSheet.sprite_width_pixels]<br />field or the<br />[SpriteSheet.sprite_height_pixels][google.cloud.video.transcoder.v1.SpriteSheet.sprite_height_pixels]<br />field, but not both (the API will automatically calculate the missing<br />field).<br /><br />For portrait videos that contain horizontal ASR and rotation metadata,<br />provide the width, in pixels, per the horizontal ASR. The API calculates<br />the height per the horizontal ASR. The API detects any rotation metadata<br />and swaps the requested height and width for the output.||
|**startTimeOffset**|str|Start time in seconds, relative to the output file timeline. Determines the first sprite to pick. The default is `0s`.||
|**totalCount**|int|Total number of sprites. Create the specified number of sprites distributed evenly across the timeline of the output media. The default is 100.||

### VertexaiCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1VertexAICustomJobSpecJobSpecBaseOutputDirectory

The Cloud Storage location to store the output of this CustomJob or PipelineJob in.  In most cases, this location is because Vertex AI associates a Google Cloud Storage bucket with every pipeline run in order to store artifacts. However, some pipeline components may override this value.  If other output destination is set, self-link will be returned, and base_output_directory value will be ignored.  API users can configure AIP_BASE_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY to obtain this value. Additionally, Vertex AI will map the environment variables:  * AIP_MODEL_DIR = `<base_output_directory>/<trial_id>/model/` * AIP_CHECKPOINT_DIR = `<base_output_directory>/<trial_id>/checkpoints/` * AIP_TENSORBOARD_LOG_DIR = `<base_output_directory>/<trial_id>/logs/`

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**outputURIPrefix**|str|Required. Google Cloud Storage URI to output directory. If the uri doesn't end with '/', a '/' will be automatically appended. The directory is created if it doesn't exist.||

### VertexaiCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1VertexAICustomJobSpecJobSpecNetworkRef

Optional. The full name of the Compute Engine [network](/compute/docs/networks-and-firewalls#networks) to which the Job should be peered. For example, `projects/12345/global/networks/myVPC`. [Format](/compute/docs/reference/rest/v1/networks/insert) is of the form `projects/{project}/global/networks/{network}`. Where {project} is a project number, as in `12345`, and {network} is a network name.  To specify this field, you must have already [configured VPC Network Peering for Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/vpc-peering).  If this field is left unspecified, the job is not peered with any network.

#### Attributes

The default target value is 60 for both metrics.<br /><br />If<br />[machine_spec.accelerator_count][google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.MachineSpec.accelerator_count]<br />is 0, the autoscaling will be based on CPU utilization metric only with<br />default target value 60 if not explicitly set.<br /><br />For example, in the case of Online Prediction, if you want to override<br />target CPU utilization to 80, you should set<br />[autoscaling_metric_specs.metric_name][google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.AutoscalingMetricSpec.metric_name]<br />to `aiplatform.googleapis.com/prediction/online/cpu/utilization` and<br />[autoscaling_metric_specs.target][google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.AutoscalingMetricSpec.target]<br />to `80`.||

If the requested value is too large, the<br />deployment will error, but if deployment succeeds then the ability to scale<br />to that many replicas is guaranteed (barring service outages). | name | type | description | default value |

If non of them exists, skip anomaly detection and only generate a statistics.<br />* MOST_RECENT_SNAPSHOT_STATS: Use the statistics generated by the most recent snapshot analysis if exists.<br />* PREVIOUS_IMPORT_FEATURES_STATS: Use the statistics generated by the previous import features analysis if exists.||
|**state**|str|Whether to enable / disable / inherite default hebavior for import features analysis. The value must be one of the values below:<br />* DEFAULT: The default behavior of whether to enable the monitoring. EntityType-level config: disabled.<br />* ENABLED: Explicitly enables import features analysis. ### VertexaiCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1VertexAIIndexSpecMetadataConfig

Immutable. The configuration of the Matching Engine Index.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

|**approximateNeighborsCount**|int|The default number of neighbors to find via approximate search before exact reordering is<br />performed. Exact reordering is a procedure where results returned by an<br />approximate search algorithm are reordered via a more expensive distance computation.<br />Required if tree-AH algorithm is used.||
|**dimensions** `required`|int|The number of dimensions of the input vectors.||
|**distanceMeasureType**|str|The distance measure used in nearest neighbor search. The value must be one of the followings:<br />* SQUARED_L2_DISTANCE: Euclidean (L_2) Distance<br />* L1_DISTANCE: Manhattan (L_1) Distance<br />* COSINE_DISTANCE: Cosine Distance. Defined as 1 - cosine similarity.<br />* DOT_PRODUCT_DISTANCE: Dot Product Distance. Defined as a negative of the dot product.||
|**featureNormType**|str|Type of normalization to be carried out on each vector. The value must be one of the followings:<br />* UNIT_L2_NORM: Unit L2 normalization type<br />* NONE: No normalization type is specified.||
|**shardSize**|str|Immutable. Index data is split into equal parts to be processed. These are called "shards".<br />The shard size must be specified when creating an index. The value must be one of the followings:<br />* SHARD_SIZE_SMALL: Small (2GB)<br />* SHARD_SIZE_MEDIUM: Medium (20GB)<br />* SHARD_SIZE_LARGE: Large (50GB).||

### VisionaiCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1VisionAIApplicationSpecApplicationConfigsNodesItems0NodeConfigBigQueryConfig

Configs of BigQuery processor.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**cloudFunctionMapping**|{str:str}|Data Schema<br />By default, Vision AI Application will try to write annotations to the<br />target BigQuery table using the following schema:<br /><br />ingestion_time: TIMESTAMP, the ingestion time of the original data.<br /><br />application: STRING, name of the application which produces the annotation.<br /><br />instance: STRING, Id of the instance which produces the annotation.<br /><br />node: STRING, name of the application graph node which produces the<br />annotation.<br /><br />annotation: STRING or JSON, the actual annotation protobuf will be<br />converted to json string with bytes field as 64 encoded string. It can be<br />written to both String or Json type column.<br /><br />To forward annotation data to an existing BigQuery table, customer needs to<br />make sure the compatibility of the schema.<br />The map maps application node name to its corresponding cloud function<br />endpoint to transform the annotations directly to the<br />google.cloud.bigquery.storage.v1.AppendRowsRequest (only avro_rows or<br />proto_rows should be set). If configured, annotations produced by<br />corresponding application node will sent to the Cloud Function at first<br />before be forwarded to BigQuery.<br /><br />If the default table schema doesn't fit, customer is able to transform the<br />annotation output from Vision AI Application to arbitrary BigQuery table<br />schema with CloudFunction.<br />* The cloud function will receive AppPlatformCloudFunctionRequest where<br />the annotations field will be the json format of Vision AI annotation.<br />* The cloud function should return AppPlatformCloudFunctionResponse with<br />AppendRowsRequest stored in the annotations field.<br />* To drop the annotation, simply clear the annotations field in the<br />returned AppPlatformCloudFunctionResponse.||
|**createDefaultTableIfNotExists**|bool|If true, App Platform will create the BigQuery DataSet and the BigQuery Table with default schema if the specified table doesn't exist. This doesn't work if any cloud function customized schema is specified since the system doesn't know your desired schema. JSON column will be used in the default table created by App Platform.||

By default, the custom processor will *not* send any data to the Vertex Prediction container. ### VisionaiCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1VisionAIApplicationSpecApplicationConfigsNodesItems0NodeConfigVertexCustomConfigDedicatedResources

A description of resources that are dedicated to the DeployedModel, and that need a higher degree of manual configuration.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**autoscalingMetricSpecs**|[[VisionaiCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1VisionAIApplicationSpecApplicationConfigsNodesItems0NodeConfigVertexCustomConfigDedicatedResourcesAutoscalingMetricSpecsItems0](#visionaicnrmcloudgooglecomv1alpha1visionaiapplicationspecapplicationconfigsnodesitems0nodeconfigvertexcustomconfigdedicatedresourcesautoscalingmetricspecsitems0)]|Immutable. The metric specifications that overrides a resource<br />utilization metric (CPU utilization, accelerator's duty cycle, and so on)<br />target value (default to 60 if not set). At most one entry is allowed per<br />metric.<br /><br />If<br />[machine_spec.accelerator_count][google.cloud.visionai.v1.MachineSpec.accelerator_count]<br />is above 0, the autoscaling will be based on both CPU utilization and<br />accelerator's duty cycle metrics and scale up when either metrics exceeds<br />its target value while scale down if both metrics are under their target<br />value. The default target value is 60 for both metrics.<br /><br />If<br />[machine_spec.accelerator_count][google.cloud.visionai.v1.MachineSpec.accelerator_count]<br />is 0, the autoscaling will be based on CPU utilization metric only with<br />default target value 60 if not explicitly set.<br /><br />For example, in the case of Online Prediction, if you want to override<br />target CPU utilization to 80, you should set<br />[autoscaling_metric_specs.metric_name][google.cloud.visionai.v1.AutoscalingMetricSpec.metric_name]<br />to `aiplatform.googleapis.com/prediction/online/cpu/utilization` and<br />[autoscaling_metric_specs.target][google.cloud.visionai.v1.AutoscalingMetricSpec.target]<br />to `80`.||
|**machineSpec**|[VisionaiCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1VisionAIApplicationSpecApplicationConfigsNodesItems0NodeConfigVertexCustomConfigDedicatedResourcesMachineSpec](#visionaicnrmcloudgooglecomv1alpha1visionaiapplicationspecapplicationconfigsnodesitems0nodeconfigvertexcustomconfigdedicatedresourcesmachinespec)|machine spec||
|**maxReplicaCount**|int|Immutable. The maximum number of replicas this DeployedModel may be<br />deployed on when the traffic against it increases. If the requested value<br />is too large, the deployment will error, but if deployment succeeds then<br />the ability to scale the model to that many replicas is guaranteed (barring<br />service outages). If traffic against the DeployedModel increases beyond<br />what its replicas at maximum may handle, a portion of the traffic will be<br />dropped. If this value is not provided, will use<br />[min_replica_count][google.cloud.visionai.v1.DedicatedResources.min_replica_count]<br />as the default value.<br /><br />The value of this field impacts the charge against Vertex CPU and GPU<br />quotas. Specifically, you will be charged for max_replica_count *<br />number of cores in the selected machine type) and (max_replica_count *<br />number of GPUs per replica in the selected machine type).||
|**minReplicaCount**|int|Required. Immutable. The minimum number of machine replicas this<br />DeployedModel will be always deployed on. This value must be greater than<br />or equal to 1.<br /><br />If traffic against the DeployedModel increases, it may dynamically be<br />deployed onto more replicas, and as traffic decreases, some of these extra<br />replicas may be freed.||

The specified IP addresses must have reserved external IP addresses in the scope of the parent network policy. To match all external IP addresses in the scope of the parent network policy, specify `0.0.0.0/0`. To match a specific external IP address, specify it using the `IpRange.external_address` property.||
|**destinationPorts**|[str]|A list of destination ports to which the external access rule applies. This field is only applicable for the UDP or TCP protocol. Each entry must be either an integer or a range. For example: `["22"]`, `["80","443"]`, or `["12345-12349"]`. To match all destination ports, specify `["0-65535"]`.||

|**priority**|int|External access rule priority, which determines the external access rule to use when multiple rules apply. If multiple rules have the same priority, their ordering is non-deterministic. If specific ordering is required, assign unique priorities to enforce such ordering. The external access rule priority is an integer from 100 to 4096, both inclusive. Lower integers indicate higher precedence. For example, a rule with priority `100` has higher precedence than a rule with priority `101`.||
|**resourceID**|str|The VMwareEngineExternalAccessRule name. If not given, the metadata.name will be used.||
|**sourceIPRanges**|[[VmwareengineCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1VMwareEngineExternalAccessRuleSpecSourceIPRangesItems0](#vmwareenginecnrmcloudgooglecomv1alpha1vmwareengineexternalaccessrulespecsourceiprangesitems0)]|If source ranges are specified, the external access rule applies only to traffic that has a source IP address in these ranges. These ranges can either be expressed in the CIDR format or as an IP address. As only inbound rules are supported, `ExternalAddress` resources cannot be the source IP addresses of an external access rule. To match all source addresses, specify `0.0.0.0/0`.||
|**sourcePorts**|[str]|A list of source ports to which the external access rule applies. This field is only applicable for the UDP or TCP protocol. Each entry must be either an integer or a range. For example: `["22"]`, `["80","443"]`, or `["12345-12349"]`. To match all source ports, specify `["0-65535"]`.||

### WorkstationsCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1WorkstationConfigSpecEncryptionKey

Immutable. Encrypts resources of this workstation configuration using a customer-managed encryption key (CMEK).  If specified, the boot disk of the Compute Engine instance and the persistent disk are encrypted using this encryption key. If this field is not set, the disks are encrypted using a generated key. Customer-managed encryption keys do not protect disk metadata.  If the customer-managed encryption key is rotated, when the workstation instance is stopped, the system attempts to recreate the persistent disk with the new version of the key. Be sure to keep older versions of the key until the persistent disk is recreated. Otherwise, data on the persistent disk might be lost.  If the encryption key is revoked, the workstation session automatically stops within 7 hours.  Immutable after the workstation configuration is created.

|**serviceAccountRef**|[WorkstationsCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1WorkstationConfigSpecEncryptionKeyServiceAccountRef](#workstationscnrmcloudgooglecomv1alpha1workstationconfigspecencryptionkeyserviceaccountref)|service account ref||

### WorkstationsCnrmCloudGoogleComV1alpha1WorkstationConfigSpecHostGceInstanceServiceAccountRef

Optional. A reference to the service account for Cloud Workstations VMs created with this configuration. When specified, be sure that the service account has `logginglogEntries.create` permission on the project so it can write logs out to Cloud Logging. If using a custom container image, the service account must have permissions to pull the specified image.  If you as the administrator want to be able to `ssh` into the underlying VM, you need to set this value to a service account for which you have the `iam.serviceAccounts.actAs` permission. Conversely, if you don't want anyone to be able to `ssh` into the underlying VM, use a service account where no one has that permission.  If not set, VMs run with a service account provided by the Cloud Workstations service, and the image must be publicly accessible.

### AccesscontextmanagerCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1AccessContextManagerServicePerimeterSpec

AccessContextManagerServicePerimeterSpec defines the desired state of AccessContextManagerServicePerimeter

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**accessPolicyRef** `required`|[AccesscontextmanagerCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1AccessContextManagerServicePerimeterSpecAccessPolicyRef](#accesscontextmanagercnrmcloudgooglecomv1beta1accesscontextmanagerserviceperimeterspecaccesspolicyref)|access policy ref||
|**description**|str|Description of the ServicePerimeter and its use. Does not affect behavior.||
|**perimeterType**|str|Immutable. Specifies the type of the Perimeter. There are two types: regular and<br />bridge. Regular Service Perimeter contains resources, access levels,<br />and restricted services. Every resource can be in at most<br />ONE regular Service Perimeter.<br /><br />In addition to being in a regular service perimeter, a resource can also<br />be in zero or more perimeter bridges. A perimeter bridge only contains<br />resources. Cross project operations are permitted if all effected<br />resources share some perimeter (whether bridge or regular). Perimeter<br />Bridge does not contain access levels or services: those are governed<br />entirely by the regular perimeter that resource is in.<br /><br />Perimeter Bridges are typically useful when building more complex<br />topologies with many independent perimeters that need to share some data<br />with a common perimeter, but should not be able to share data among<br />themselves. Default value: "PERIMETER_TYPE_REGULAR" Possible values: ["PERIMETER_TYPE_REGULAR", "PERIMETER_TYPE_BRIDGE"].||
|**resourceID**|str|Immutable. Optional. The name of the resource. Used for creation and acquisition. When unset, the value of `metadata.name` is used as the default.||
|**spec**|[AccesscontextmanagerCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1AccessContextManagerServicePerimeterSpecSpec](#accesscontextmanagercnrmcloudgooglecomv1beta1accesscontextmanagerserviceperimeterspecspec)|spec||
|**status**|[AccesscontextmanagerCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1AccessContextManagerServicePerimeterSpecStatus](#accesscontextmanagercnrmcloudgooglecomv1beta1accesscontextmanagerserviceperimeterspecstatus)|status||
|**title** `required`|str|Human readable title. Must be unique within the Policy.||
|**useExplicitDryRunSpec**|bool|Use explicit dry run spec flag. Ordinarily, a dry-run spec implicitly exists for all Service Perimeters, and that spec is identical to the status for those Service Perimeters. When this flag is set, it inhibits the generation of the implicit spec, thereby allowing the user to explicitly provide a configuration ("spec") to use in a dry-run version of the Service Perimeter. This allows the user to test changes to the enforced config ("status") without actually enforcing them. This testing is done through analyzing the differences between currently enforced and suggested restrictions. useExplicitDryRunSpec must bet set to True if any of the fields in the spec are set to non-default values.||

AccessLevels listed must be in the same policy as this ServicePerimeter. Referencing a nonexistent AccessLevel is a syntax error. If no AccessLevel names are listed, resources within the perimeter can only be accessed via GCP calls with request origins within the perimeter. For Service Perimeter Bridge, must be empty.||
|**egressPolicies**|[[AccesscontextmanagerCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1AccessContextManagerServicePerimeterSpecSpecEgressPoliciesItems0](#accesscontextmanagercnrmcloudgooglecomv1beta1accesscontextmanagerserviceperimeterspecspecegresspoliciesitems0)]|List of EgressPolicies to apply to the perimeter. Currently only projects are allowed.||

### AlloydbCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1AlloyDBClusterSpecAutomatedBackupPolicy

The automated backup policy for this cluster.  If no policy is provided then the default policy will be used. If backups are supported for the cluster, the default policy takes one backup a day, has a backup window of 1 hour, and retains backups for 14 days. For more information on the defaults, consult the documentation for the message type.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**backupWindow**|str|The length of the time window during which a backup can be<br />taken. If a backup does not succeed within this time window, it will be<br />canceled and considered failed.<br /><br />The backup window must be at least 5 minutes long. There is no upper bound<br />on the window. If not set, it defaults to 1 hour.||
|**enabled**|bool|Whether automated automated backups are enabled. If not set, defaults to true.||
|**encryptionConfig**|[AlloydbCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1AlloyDBClusterSpecAutomatedBackupPolicyEncryptionConfig](#alloydbcnrmcloudgooglecomv1beta1alloydbclusterspecautomatedbackuppolicyencryptionconfig)|encryption config||
|**labels**|{str:str}|Labels to apply to backups created using this configuration.||
|**location**|str|The location where the backup will be stored. Currently, the only supported<br />option is to store the backup in the same region as the cluster.<br /><br />If empty, defaults to the region of the cluster.||
|**quantityBasedRetention**|[AlloydbCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1AlloyDBClusterSpecAutomatedBackupPolicyQuantityBasedRetention](#alloydbcnrmcloudgooglecomv1beta1alloydbclusterspecautomatedbackuppolicyquantitybasedretention)|quantity based retention||
|**timeBasedRetention**|[AlloydbCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1AlloyDBClusterSpecAutomatedBackupPolicyTimeBasedRetention](#alloydbcnrmcloudgooglecomv1beta1alloydbclusterspecautomatedbackuppolicytimebasedretention)|time based retention||
|**weeklySchedule**|[AlloydbCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1AlloyDBClusterSpecAutomatedBackupPolicyWeeklySchedule](#alloydbcnrmcloudgooglecomv1beta1alloydbclusterspecautomatedbackuppolicyweeklyschedule)|weekly schedule||

### AlloydbCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1AlloyDBInstanceSpecInstanceTypeRef

The type of instance. Possible values: ["PRIMARY", "READ_POOL", "SECONDARY"]  For PRIMARY and SECONDARY instances, set the value to refer to the name of the associated cluster. This is recommended because the instance type of primary and secondary instances is tied to the cluster type of the associated cluster. If the secondary cluster is promoted to primary cluster, then the associated secondary instance also becomes primary instance. Example: instanceTypeRef: name: clusterName For instances of type READ_POOL, set the value using external keyword. Example: instanceTypeRef: external: READ_POOL If the instance type is SECONDARY, the delete instance operation does not delete the secondary instance but abandons it instead. Use deletionPolicy = "FORCE" in the associated secondary cluster and delete the cluster forcefully to delete the secondary cluster as well its associated secondary instance.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**external**|str|The type of instance. Possible values: ["PRIMARY", "READ_POOL", "SECONDARY"]||

|**namespace**|str|The `metadata.namespace` field of a `AlloyDBCluster` resource.||

### ApigeeCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1ApigeeOrganizationSpecAuthorizedNetworkRef

Compute Engine network used for Service Networking to be peered with Apigee runtime instances. See [Getting started with the Service Networking API](https://cloud.google.com/service-infrastructure/docs/service-networking/getting-started). Valid only when [RuntimeType](#RuntimeType) is set to `CLOUD`. The value must be set before the creation of a runtime instance and can be updated only when there are no runtime instances. For example: `default`. Apigee also supports shared VPC (that is, the host network project is not the same as the one that is peering with Apigee). See [Shared VPC overview](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/shared-vpc). To use a shared VPC network, use the following format: `projects/{host-project-id}/{region}/networks/{network-name}`. For example: `projects/my-sharedvpc-host/global/networks/mynetwork` **Note:** Not supported for Apigee hybrid.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**external**|str|A reference to an externally managed ComputeNetwork resource. Should be in the format "projects/{{projectID}}/global/networks/{{networkID}}".||
|**name**|str|The name of a ComputeNetwork resource.||
|**namespace**|str|The namespace of a ComputeNetwork resource.||

### AssetCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1AssetFeedSpecCondition

A condition which determines whether an asset update should be published. If specified, an asset will be returned only when the expression evaluates to true. When set, `expression` field in the `Expr` must be a valid [CEL expression] (https://github.com/google/cel-spec) on a TemporalAsset with name `temporal_asset`. Example: a Feed with expression ("temporal_asset.deleted == true") will only publish Asset deletions. Other fields of `Expr` are optional.  See our [user guide](https://cloud.google.com/asset-inventory/docs/monitoring-asset-changes-with-condition) for detailed instructions.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**description**|str|Optional. Description of the expression. This is a longer text which describes the expression, e.g. when hovered over it in a UI.||
|**expression**|str|Textual representation of an expression in Common Expression Language syntax.||
|**location**|str|Optional. String indicating the location of the expression for error reporting, e.g. a file name and a position in the file.||
|**title**|str|Optional. Title for the expression, i.e. a short string describing its purpose. This can be used e.g. in UIs which allow to enter the expression.||

### AssetCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1AssetSavedQuerySpecContentIamPolicyAnalysisQueryOptions

Optional. The query options.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**analyzeServiceAccountImpersonation**|bool|Optional. If true, the response will include access analysis from<br />identities to resources via service account impersonation. This is a very<br />expensive operation, because many derived queries will be executed. We<br />highly recommend you use<br />[AssetService.AnalyzeIamPolicyLongrunning][google.cloud.asset.v1.AssetService.AnalyzeIamPolicyLongrunning]<br />RPC instead.<br /><br />For example, if the request analyzes for which resources user A has<br />permission P, and there's an IAM policy states user A has<br />iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken permission to a service account SA,<br />and there's another IAM policy states service account SA has permission P<br />to a Google Cloud folder F, then user A potentially has access to the<br />Google Cloud folder F. And those advanced analysis results will be<br />included in<br />[AnalyzeIamPolicyResponse.service_account_impersonation_analysis][google.cloud.asset.v1.AnalyzeIamPolicyResponse.service_account_impersonation_analysis].<br /><br />Another example, if the request analyzes for who has<br />permission P to a Google Cloud folder F, and there's an IAM policy states<br />user A has iam.serviceAccounts.actAs permission to a service account SA,<br />and there's another IAM policy states service account SA has permission P<br />to the Google Cloud folder F, then user A potentially has access to the<br />Google Cloud folder F. And those advanced analysis results will be<br />included in<br />[AnalyzeIamPolicyResponse.service_account_impersonation_analysis][google.cloud.asset.v1.AnalyzeIamPolicyResponse.service_account_impersonation_analysis].<br /><br />Only the following permissions are considered in this analysis:<br /><br />* `iam.serviceAccounts.actAs`<br />* `iam.serviceAccounts.signBlob`<br />* `iam.serviceAccounts.signJwt`<br />* `iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken`<br />* `iam.serviceAccounts.getOpenIdToken`<br />* `iam.serviceAccounts.implicitDelegation`<br /><br />Default is false.||
|**expandGroups**|bool|Optional. If true, the identities section of the result will expand any<br />Google groups appearing in an IAM policy binding.<br /><br />If<br />[IamPolicyAnalysisQuery.identity_selector][google.cloud.asset.v1.IamPolicyAnalysisQuery.identity_selector]<br />is specified, the identity in the result will be determined by the<br />selector, and this flag is not allowed to set.<br /><br />If true, the default max expansion per group is 1000 for<br />AssetService.AnalyzeIamPolicy][].<br /><br />Default is false.||
|**expandResources**|bool|Optional. If true and<br />[IamPolicyAnalysisQuery.resource_selector][google.cloud.asset.v1.IamPolicyAnalysisQuery.resource_selector]<br />is not specified, the resource section of the result will expand any<br />resource attached to an IAM policy to include resources lower in the<br />resource hierarchy.<br /><br />For example, if the request analyzes for which resources user A has<br />permission P, and the results include an IAM policy with P on a Google<br />Cloud folder, the results will also include resources in that folder with<br />permission P.<br /><br />If true and<br />[IamPolicyAnalysisQuery.resource_selector][google.cloud.asset.v1.IamPolicyAnalysisQuery.resource_selector]<br />is specified, the resource section of the result will expand the<br />specified resource to include resources lower in the resource hierarchy.<br />Only project or lower resources are supported. Folder and organization<br />resources cannot be used together with this option.<br /><br />For example, if the request analyzes for which users have permission P on<br />a Google Cloud project with this option enabled, the results will include<br />all users who have permission P on that project or any lower resource.<br /><br />If true, the default max expansion per resource is 1000 for<br />AssetService.AnalyzeIamPolicy][] and 100000 for<br />AssetService.AnalyzeIamPolicyLongrunning][].<br /><br />Default is false.||
|**expandRoles**|bool|Optional. If true, the access section of result will expand any roles<br />appearing in IAM policy bindings to include their permissions.<br /><br />If<br />[IamPolicyAnalysisQuery.access_selector][google.cloud.asset.v1.IamPolicyAnalysisQuery.access_selector]<br />is specified, the access section of the result will be determined by the<br />selector, and this flag is not allowed to set.<br /><br />Default is false.||
|**outputGroupEdges**|bool|Optional. If true, the result will output the relevant membership relationships between groups and other groups, and between groups and principals. Default is false.||
|**outputResourceEdges**|bool|Optional. If true, the result will output the relevant parent/child relationships between resources. Default is false.||

### BackupdrCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1BackupDRBackupPlanSpecBackupRulesItems0StandardSchedule

Optional. Defines a schedule that runs within the confines of a defined window of time.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**backupWindow**|[BackupdrCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1BackupDRBackupPlanSpecBackupRulesItems0StandardScheduleBackupWindow](#backupdrcnrmcloudgooglecomv1beta1backupdrbackupplanspecbackuprulesitems0standardschedulebackupwindow)|backup window||
|**daysOfMonth**|[int]|Optional. Specifies days of months like 1, 5, or 14 on which jobs will run.<br /><br />Values for `days_of_month` are only applicable for `recurrence_type`,<br />`MONTHLY` and `YEARLY`. A validation error will occur if other values are<br />supplied.||
|**daysOfWeek**|[str]|Optional. Specifies days of week like, MONDAY or TUESDAY, on which jobs<br />will run.<br /><br />This is required for `recurrence_type`, `WEEKLY` and is not applicable<br />otherwise. A validation error will occur if a value is supplied and<br />`recurrence_type` is not `WEEKLY`.||
|**hourlyFrequency**|int|Optional. Specifies frequency for hourly backups. A hourly frequency of 2<br />means jobs will run every 2 hours from start time till end time defined.<br /><br />This is required for `recurrence_type`, `HOURLY` and is not applicable<br />otherwise. A validation error will occur if a value is supplied and<br />`recurrence_type` is not `HOURLY`.<br /><br />Value of hourly frequency should be between 4 and 23.<br /><br />Reason for limit : We found that there is bandwidth limitation of 3GB/S for<br />GMI while taking a backup and 5GB/S while doing a restore. Given the amount<br />of parallel backups and restore we are targeting, this will potentially<br />take the backup time to mins and hours (in worst case scenario).||
|**months**|[str]|Optional. Specifies the months of year, like `FEBRUARY` and/or `MAY`, on<br />which jobs will run.<br /><br />This field is only applicable when `recurrence_type` is `YEARLY`. A<br />validation error will occur if other values are supplied.||
|**recurrenceType**|str|Required. Specifies the `RecurrenceType` for the schedule.||
|**timeZone**|str|Required. The time zone to be used when interpreting the schedule. The value of this field must be a time zone name from the IANA tz database. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones for the list of valid timezone names. For e.g., Europe/Paris.||
|**weekDayOfMonth**|[BackupdrCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1BackupDRBackupPlanSpecBackupRulesItems0StandardScheduleWeekDayOfMonth](#backupdrcnrmcloudgooglecomv1beta1backupdrbackupplanspecbackuprulesitems0standardscheduleweekdayofmonth)|week day of month||
### BackupdrCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1BackupDRBackupPlanSpecBackupRulesItems0StandardScheduleBackupWindow

Required. A BackupWindow defines the window of day during which backup jobs will run. Jobs are queued at the beginning of the window and will be marked as `NOT_RUN` if they do not start by the end of the window.  Note: running jobs will not be cancelled at the end of the window.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**endHourOfDay**|int|Required. The hour of day (1-24) when the window end for e.g. if value of<br />end hour of day is 10 that mean backup window end time is 10:00.<br /><br />End hour of day should be greater than start hour of day.<br />0 <= start_hour_of_day < end_hour_of_day <= 24<br /><br />End hour of day is not include in backup window that mean if<br />end_hour_of_day= 10 jobs should start before 10:00.||
|**startHourOfDay**|int|Required. The hour of day (0-23) when the window starts for e.g. if value of start hour of day is 6 that mean backup window start at 6:00.||
### BackupdrCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1BackupDRBackupPlanSpecBackupRulesItems0StandardScheduleWeekDayOfMonth

Optional. Specifies a week day of the month like, FIRST SUNDAY or LAST MONDAY, on which jobs will run. This will be specified by two fields in `WeekDayOfMonth`, one for the day, e.g. `MONDAY`, and one for the week, e.g. `LAST`.  This field is only applicable for `recurrence_type`, `MONTHLY` and `YEARLY`. A validation error will occur if other values are supplied.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**dayOfWeek**|str|Required. Specifies the day of the week.||
|**weekOfMonth**|str|Required. Specifies the week of the month.||

The missing values are treated as nulls.<br />If false, records with missing trailing columns are treated as bad records, and if there are too many bad records,<br />an invalid error is returned in the job result. The default value is false. Only applicable to CSV, ignored for other formats.||
|**allowQuotedNewlines**|bool|Immutable. Indicates if BigQuery should allow quoted data sections that contain newline characters in a CSV file.<br />The default value is false.||
|**autodetect**|bool|Immutable. Indicates if we should automatically infer the options and schema for CSV and JSON sources.||
|**createDisposition**|str|Immutable. Specifies whether the job is allowed to create new tables. The following values are supported:<br />CREATE_IF_NEEDED: If the table does not exist, BigQuery creates the table.<br />CREATE_NEVER: The table must already exist. If it does not, a 'notFound' error is returned in the job result.<br />Creation, truncation and append actions occur as one atomic update upon job completion Default value: "CREATE_NEVER" Possible values: ["CREATE_IF_NEEDED", "CREATE_NEVER"].||
|**destinationEncryptionConfiguration**|[BigqueryCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1BigQueryJobSpecLoadDestinationEncryptionConfiguration](#bigquerycnrmcloudgooglecomv1beta1bigqueryjobspecloaddestinationencryptionconfiguration)|destination encryption configuration||

|**encoding**|str|Immutable. The character encoding of the data. The supported values are UTF-8 or ISO-8859-1.<br />The default value is UTF-8. BigQuery decodes the data after the raw, binary data<br />has been split using the values of the quote and fieldDelimiter properties.||
|**fieldDelimiter**|str|Immutable. The separator for fields in a CSV file. The separator can be any ISO-8859-1 single-byte character.<br />To use a character in the range 128-255, you must encode the character as UTF8. BigQuery converts<br />the string to ISO-8859-1 encoding, and then uses the first byte of the encoded string to split the<br />data in its raw, binary state. BigQuery also supports the escape sequence "\t" to specify a tab separator.<br />The default value is a comma (',').||
|**ignoreUnknownValues**|bool|Immutable. Indicates if BigQuery should allow extra values that are not represented in the table schema.<br />If true, the extra values are ignored. If false, records with extra columns are treated as bad records,<br />and if there are too many bad records, an invalid error is returned in the job result.<br />The default value is false. The sourceFormat property determines what BigQuery treats as an extra value:<br />CSV: Trailing columns<br />JSON: Named values that don't match any column names.||
|**jsonExtension**|str|Immutable. If sourceFormat is set to newline-delimited JSON, indicates whether it should be processed as a JSON variant such as GeoJSON.<br />For a sourceFormat other than JSON, omit this field. If the sourceFormat is newline-delimited JSON: - for newline-delimited<br />GeoJSON: set to GEOJSON.||
|**maxBadRecords**|int|Immutable. The maximum number of bad records that BigQuery can ignore when running the job. If the number of bad records exceeds this value,<br />an invalid error is returned in the job result. The default value is 0, which requires that all records are valid.||
|**nullMarker**|str|Immutable. Specifies a string that represents a null value in a CSV file. For example, if you specify "\N", BigQuery interprets "\N" as a null value<br />when loading a CSV file. The default value is the empty string. If you set this property to a custom value, BigQuery throws an error if an<br />empty string is present for all data types except for STRING and BYTE. For STRING and BYTE columns, BigQuery interprets the empty string as<br />an empty value.||

|**projectionFields**|[str]|Immutable. If no properties are specified, BigQuery loads all properties.<br />If any named property isn't found in the Cloud Datastore backup, an invalid error is returned in the job result.||
|**quote**|str|Immutable. The value that is used to quote data sections in a CSV file. BigQuery converts the string to ISO-8859-1 encoding,<br />and then uses the first byte of the encoded string to split the data in its raw, binary state.<br />The default value is a double-quote ('"'). If your data does not contain quoted sections, set the property value to an empty string.<br />If your data contains quoted newline characters, you must also set the allowQuotedNewlines property to true.||
|**schemaUpdateOptions**|[str]|Immutable. Allows the schema of the destination table to be updated as a side effect of the load job if a schema is autodetected or<br />supplied in the job configuration. Schema update options are supported in two cases: when writeDisposition is WRITE_APPEND;<br />when writeDisposition is WRITE_TRUNCATE and the destination table is a partition of a table, specified by partition decorators.<br />For normal tables, WRITE_TRUNCATE will always overwrite the schema. One or more of the following values are specified:<br />ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION: allow adding a nullable field to the schema.<br />ALLOW_FIELD_RELAXATION: allow relaxing a required field in the original schema to nullable.||
|**skipLeadingRows**|int|Immutable. The number of rows at the top of a CSV file that BigQuery will skip when loading the data.<br />The default value is 0. This property is useful if you have header rows in the file that should be skipped.<br />When autodetect is on, the behavior is the following:<br />skipLeadingRows unspecified - Autodetect tries to detect headers in the first row. If they are not detected,<br />the row is read as data. Otherwise data is read starting from the second row.<br />skipLeadingRows is 0 - Instructs autodetect that there are no headers and data should be read starting from the first row.<br />skipLeadingRows = N > 0 - Autodetect skips N-1 rows and tries to detect headers in row N. If headers are not detected,<br />row N is just skipped. Otherwise row N is used to extract column names for the detected schema.||
|**sourceFormat**|str|Immutable. The format of the data files. For CSV files, specify "CSV". |**sourceUris** `required`|[str]|Immutable. The fully-qualified URIs that point to your data in Google Cloud.<br />For Google Cloud Storage URIs: Each URI can contain one '\*' wildcard character<br />and it must come after the 'bucket' name. Size limits related to load jobs apply<br />to external data sources. For Google Cloud Bigtable URIs: Exactly one URI can be<br />specified and it has be a fully specified and valid HTTPS URL for a Google Cloud Bigtable table.<br />For Google Cloud Datastore backups: Exactly one URI can be specified. |**timePartitioning**|[BigqueryCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1BigQueryJobSpecLoadTimePartitioning](#bigquerycnrmcloudgooglecomv1beta1bigqueryjobspecloadtimepartitioning)|time partitioning||
|**writeDisposition**|str|Immutable. Specifies the action that occurs if the destination table already exists. The following values are supported:<br />WRITE_TRUNCATE: If the table already exists, BigQuery overwrites the table data and uses the schema from the query result.<br />WRITE_APPEND: If the table already exists, BigQuery appends the data to the table.<br />WRITE_EMPTY: If the table already exists and contains data, a 'duplicate' error is returned in the job result.<br />Each action is atomic and only occurs if BigQuery is able to complete the job successfully.<br />Creation, truncation and append actions occur as one atomic update upon job completion. Default value: "WRITE_EMPTY" Possible values: ["WRITE_TRUNCATE", "WRITE_APPEND", "WRITE_EMPTY"].||

The sourceFormat property determines what BigQuery treats as an extra value: CSV: Trailing columns JSON: Named values that don't match any column names Google Cloud Bigtable: This setting is ignored. Google Cloud Datastore backups: This setting is ignored. Avro: This setting is ignored. ORC: This setting is ignored. Parquet: This setting is ignored.||

### BigqueryCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1BigQueryTableSpecExternalDataConfigurationCsvOptions

Additional properties to set if sourceFormat is set to CSV.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**allowJaggedRows**|bool|Indicates if BigQuery should accept rows that are missing trailing optional columns. If true, BigQuery treats missing trailing columns as null values. If false, records with missing trailing columns are treated as bad records, and if there are too many bad records, an invalid error is returned in the job result. The default value is false.||
|**allowQuotedNewlines**|bool|Indicates if BigQuery should allow quoted data sections that contain newline characters in a CSV file. The default value is false.||
|**encoding**|str|The character encoding of the data. The supported values are UTF-8, ISO-8859-1, UTF-16BE, UTF-16LE, UTF-32BE, and UTF-32LE.  The default value is UTF-8. BigQuery decodes the data after the raw, binary data has been split using the values of the quote and fieldDelimiter properties.||
|**fieldDelimiter**|str|The separator character for fields in a CSV file. The separator is interpreted as a single byte. For files encoded in ISO-8859-1, any single character can be used as a separator. For files encoded in UTF-8, characters represented in decimal range 1-127 (U+0001-U+007F) can be used without any modification. UTF-8 characters encoded with multiple bytes (i.e. U+0080 and above) will have only the first byte used for separating fields. The remaining bytes will be treated as a part of the field. BigQuery also supports the escape sequence "\t" (U+0009) to specify a tab separator. The default value is comma (",", U+002C).||
|**quote** `required`|str|The value that is used to quote data sections in a CSV file. BigQuery converts the string to ISO-8859-1 encoding, and then uses the first byte of the encoded string to split the data in its raw, binary state. The default value is a double-quote ("). If your data does not contain quoted sections, set the property value to an empty string. If your data contains quoted newline characters, you must also set the allowQuotedNewlines property to true. To include the specific quote character within a quoted value, precede it with an additional matching quote character. For example, if you want to escape the default character  ' " ', use ' "" '.||
|**skipLeadingRows**|int|The number of rows at the top of a CSV file that BigQuery will<br />skip when reading the data. The default value is 0. This property is<br />useful if you have header rows in the file that should be skipped.<br />When autodetect is on, the behavior is the following:<br /><br />* skipLeadingRows unspecified - Autodetect tries to detect headers in the<br />first row. If they are not detected, the row is read as data. Otherwise<br />data is read starting from the second row.<br />* skipLeadingRows is 0 - Instructs autodetect that there are no headers and<br />data should be read starting from the first row.<br />* skipLeadingRows = N > 0 - Autodetect skips N-1 rows and tries to detect<br />headers in row N. If headers are not detected, row N is just skipped.<br />Otherwise row N is used to extract column names for the detected schema.||
### BigqueryCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1BigQueryTableSpecExternalDataConfigurationGoogleSheetsOptions

Additional options if sourceFormat is set to GOOGLE_SHEETS.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**range**|str|Range of a sheet to query from. Only used when non-empty. Typical format: sheet_name!top_left_cell_id:bottom_right_cell_id For example: sheet1!A1:B20||
|**skipLeadingRows**|int|The number of rows at the top of a sheet that BigQuery will skip when reading the data. The default value is 0. This property is useful if you have header rows that should be skipped. When autodetect is on, the behavior is the following: * skipLeadingRows unspecified - Autodetect tries to detect headers in the first row. If they are not detected, the row is read as data. Otherwise data is read starting from the second row. * skipLeadingRows is 0 - Instructs autodetect that there are no headers and data should be read starting from the first row. * skipLeadingRows = N > 0 - Autodetect skips N-1 rows and tries to detect headers in row N. If headers are not detected, row N is just skipped. Otherwise row N is used to extract column names for the detected schema.||
### BigqueryCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1BigQueryTableSpecExternalDataConfigurationHivePartitioningOptions

When set, configures hive partitioning support. Not all storage formats support hive partitioning -- requesting hive partitioning on an unsupported format will lead to an error, as will providing an invalid specification.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**mode**|str|When set, what mode of hive partitioning to use when reading<br />data.  The following modes are supported:<br /><br />* AUTO: automatically infer partition key name(s) and type(s).<br /><br />* STRINGS: automatically infer partition key name(s).  All types are<br />strings.<br /><br />* CUSTOM: partition key schema is encoded in the source URI prefix.<br /><br />Not all storage formats support hive partitioning. Requesting hive<br />partitioning on an unsupported format will lead to an error.<br />Currently supported formats are: JSON, CSV, ORC, Avro and Parquet.||
|**requirePartitionFilter**|bool|If set to true, queries over this table require a partition<br />filter that can be used for partition elimination to be specified.<br /><br />Note that this field should only be true when creating a permanent<br />external table or querying a temporary external table.<br /><br />Hive-partitioned loads with require_partition_filter explicitly set to<br />true will fail.||
|**sourceUriPrefix**|str|When hive partition detection is requested, a common prefix for<br />all source uris must be required.  The prefix must end immediately before<br />the partition key encoding begins. For example, consider files following<br />this data layout:<br /><br />gs://bucket/path_to_table/dt=2019-06-01/country=USA/id=7/file.avro<br /><br />gs://bucket/path_to_table/dt=2019-05-31/country=CA/id=3/file.avro<br /><br />When hive partitioning is requested with either AUTO or STRINGS detection,<br />the common prefix can be either of gs://bucket/path_to_table or<br />gs://bucket/path_to_table/.<br /><br />CUSTOM detection requires encoding the partitioning schema immediately<br />after the common prefix.  For CUSTOM, any of<br /><br />* gs://bucket/path_to_table/{dt:DATE}/{country:STRING}/{id:INTEGER}<br /><br />* gs://bucket/path_to_table/{dt:STRING}/{country:STRING}/{id:INTEGER}<br /><br />* gs://bucket/path_to_table/{dt:DATE}/{country:STRING}/{id:STRING}<br /><br />would all be valid source URI prefixes.||

### BigtableCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1BigtableInstanceSpecClusterItems0KmsKeyRef

Describes the Cloud KMS encryption key that will be used to protect the destination Bigtable cluster. The requirements for this key are:  1) The Cloud Bigtable service account associated with the project that contains this cluster must be granted the cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter role on the CMEK key. 2) Only regional keys can be used and the region of the CMEK key must match the region of the cluster. 3) All clusters within an instance must use the same CMEK key access to this encryption key.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**external**|str|A reference to an externally managed KMSCryptoKey. Should be in the format `projects/[kms_project_id]/locations/[region]/keyRings/[key_ring_id]/cryptoKeys/[key]`.||
|**name**|str|The `name` of a `KMSCryptoKey` resource.||
|**namespace**|str|The `namespace` of a `KMSCryptoKey` resource.||

### BillingbudgetsCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1BillingBudgetsBudgetSpecAmountSpecifiedAmount

A specified amount to use as the budget. `currency_code` is optional. If specified when creating a budget, it must match the currency of the billing account. If specified when updating a budget, it must match the currency_code of the existing budget. The `currency_code` is provided on output.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**currencyCode**|str|Immutable. The three-letter currency code defined in ISO 4217.||
|**nanos**|int|Number of nano (10^-9) units of the amount. The value must be between -999,999,999 and +999,999,999 inclusive. If `units` is positive, `nanos` must be positive or zero. If `units` is zero, `nanos` can be positive, zero, or negative. If `units` is negative, `nanos` must be negative or zero. For example $-1.75 is represented as `units`=-1 and `nanos`=-750,000,000.||
|**units**|int|The whole units of the amount. For example if `currencyCode` is `"USD"`, then 1 unit is one US dollar.||

### BillingbudgetsCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1BillingBudgetsBudgetSpecBudgetFilter

Optional. Filters that define which resources are used to compute the actual spend against the budget amount, such as projects, services, and the budget's time period, as well as other filters.

#### Attributes

| name | type | description | default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|**calendarPeriod**|str|Optional. Specifies to track usage for recurring calendar period. For example, assume that CalendarPeriod.QUARTER is set. The budget will track usage from April 1 to June 30, when the current calendar month is April, May, June. After that, it will track usage from July 1 to September 30 when the current calendar month is July, August, September, so on. Possible values: CALENDAR_PERIOD_UNSPECIFIED, MONTH, QUARTER, YEAR||
|**creditTypes**|[str]|Optional. If Filter.credit_types_treatment is INCLUDE_SPECIFIED_CREDITS, this is a list of credit types to be subtracted from gross cost to determine the spend for threshold calculations. See a list of acceptable credit type values. If Filter.credit_types_treatment is not INCLUDE_SPECIFIED_CREDITS, this field must be empty.||
|**creditTypesTreatment**|str|Optional. If not set, default behavior is `INCLUDE_ALL_CREDITS`.||
|**customPeriod**|[BillingbudgetsCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1BillingBudgetsBudgetSpecBudgetFilterCustomPeriod](#billingbudgetscnrmcloudgooglecomv1beta1billingbudgetsbudgetspecbudgetfiltercustomperiod)|custom period||

If omitted, the report will include all labeled and unlabeled usage.||
|**projects**|[[BillingbudgetsCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1BillingBudgetsBudgetSpecBudgetFilterProjectsItems0](#billingbudgetscnrmcloudgooglecomv1beta1billingbudgetsbudgetspecbudgetfilterprojectsitems0)]|projects||

|**subaccounts**|[[BillingbudgetsCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1BillingBudgetsBudgetSpecBudgetFilterSubaccountsItems0](#billingbudgetscnrmcloudgooglecomv1beta1billingbudgetsbudgetspecbudgetfiltersubaccountsitems0)]|subaccounts||

Upon completion of the build, volumes and their contents<br />are discarded.<br /><br />Using a named volume in only one step is not valid as it is<br />indicative of a build request with an incorrect configuration.||

### CloudbuildCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1CloudBuildTriggerSpecTriggerTemplate

Any branch or tag change that matches that regular expression will trigger a build.  One of 'trigger_template', 'github', 'pubsub_config', 'webhook_config' or 'source_to_build' must be provided.

|**commitSha**|str|Explicit commit SHA to build. Exactly one of a branch name, tag, or commit SHA must be provided.||
|**dir**|str|Directory, relative to the source root, in which to run the build.<br /><br />This must be a relative path. If a step's dir is specified and<br />is an absolute path, this value is ignored for that step's<br />execution.||
|**invertRegex**|bool|Only trigger a build if the revision regex does NOT match the revision regex.||
|**repoRef**|[CloudbuildCnrmCloudGoogleComV1beta1CloudBuildTriggerSpecTriggerTemplateRepoRef](#cloudbuildcnrmcloudgooglecomv1beta1cloudbuildtriggerspectriggertemplatereporef)|repo ref||
|**tagName**|str|Name of the tag to build. Exactly one of a branch name, tag, or commit SHA must be provided. This field is a regular expression.||
